newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai economy can withstand VAT tax hike - Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: Thai economy can withstand VAT tax hike - Fin Min.

text.p: Thailand's economy can withstand a three percentage point increase in value added tax (VAT), finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Tuesday.

He made the comments in a nationally televised address to explain a series of tough measures announced earlier by the government to help boost the ailing economy. One of the measures was an increase in the VAT to 10 percent from seven percent, effective on August 16.

The VAT increase was recommended by the International Monetary Fund, which advised the government on the measures it needed to implement to help turn around the economy which is growing at its slowest pace in a decade.
The VAT increase was one of the more hotly-contested issues, finance officials said, because of the immediate impact it would have on the people.
Thanong told reporters earlier the VAT hike was expected to raise government revenue by more than 70 billion baht ($2.25 billion) in the 1997/98 (October-September) fiscal year.
